title: RC16 OAG (GP678C, then ZWO ASI174MM Mini; 3248 mm)

nina.note: no guider settings in the NINA profile

ascom.note: driver flag names not known yet

file.note: dark library found, defect map found

rows.label: Calibration on record (PS-93)
rows.why: Guiding on a poor calibration (09-26: ortho 15.1 deg at Dec 66.6) makes every correction partly wrong.
rows.fix: System page: Calibrate at the next dispatch (PS-93).
rows.desired: graded PASS or WARN, under phd2_cal_max_age_days

rows.label: Reverse Dec output after meridian flip
rows.why: If this does not match the mount, Dec runs away after the flip; PS-93 checks it on the first minutes after each flip.
rows.fix: Toggle Advanced > Mount > Reverse Dec output after meridian flip only after the PS-93 runaway alert.
rows.current: Dec ran away after the flip (East)
rows.note: 96.4% of Dec pulses N while the Dec error grew -1.8 -> -16 px
rows.desired: Dec holds after a meridian flip (PS-93 after-flip check)

rows.label: Guide binning
rows.why: 2x2 gives about 0.25 arcsec/px, plenty for 2 to 3 arcsec seeing, with four times the signal per pixel. The auto-tune ticket (PS-90) may change this; re-audit after.
rows.fix: Brain > Camera: binning 2.

rows.label: Guide camera gain
rows.why: Gain sets how bright the guide star reads at a 1 to 4 s exposure. The PS-90 tuner recommends it from recent nights (more gain when a filter is still faint at 4 s, less when one clips at 1 s); info until it has data.
rows.fix: Brain > Camera: camera gain as recommended (System page > Guide star). The armer writes it pre-dusk only with phd2_audit_autofix.
rows.desired: 100 (PS-90 tuner: faintest filter needs 10.9x the signal at 4000 ms: gain 90 -> 100; even gain 100 is short: bin 3 is the next step (approved: stay at bin 2 until decided from data))
rows.manual_hint: set in PHD2: Brain > Camera: camera gain as recommended (System page > Guide star). The armer writes it pre-dusk only with phd2_audit_autofix.

rows.label: Guide exposure (ms)
rows.why: 2 to 4 s averages the seeing at 3248 mm; 1 s chases seeing and 6 s reacts too slowly.
rows.fix: PHD2 exposure dropdown: 2 to 4 s.

rows.label: Search region (px)
rows.why: PHD2 searches this many pixels each side of the star; it must at least cover a dither (09-26 ran 15 px against 20 to 25 px dithers and lost the star).
rows.fix: Brain > Guiding: search region 35 px (30 to 40, and at least NINA's dither pixels).
rows.manual_hint: set in PHD2: Brain > Guiding: search region 35 px (30 to 40, and at least NINA's dither pixels).

rows.label: RA minimum move (px)
rows.why: The Guiding Assistant measures the seeing; a min-move far below it chases seeing (09-25 GA said 1.50 px, PHD2 had 0.76).
rows.fix: Use the Guiding Assistant's RA min-move.

rows.label: Dec minimum move (px)
rows.why: A Dec min-move above a few pixels leaves Dec unguided: 20 px is about 5 arcsec at 0.25"/px. Near the Guiding Assistant's RA min-move ignores seeing but still corrects drift; far below it chases the seeing.
rows.fix: Brain > Algorithms > Dec: minimum move about the Guiding Assistant's RA value (0.5 to 3 px without one).
rows.note: below the band: Dec chases the seeing
rows.desired: 0.75 to 3.00 px (0.5 to 2 x the Guiding Assistant's RA min-move 1.5), never over 5 px

rows.label: Calibration step (ms)
rows.why: About 12 steps per axis gives a good calibration; 250 ms gave only 3 steps on 09-26.
rows.fix: Brain > Guiding > Calibration step calculator (PS-93 recommends the value).
rows.manual_hint: set in PHD2: Brain > Guiding > Calibration step calculator (PS-93 recommends the value).

rows.label: PHD2 alerts not silenced
rows.why: An alert ticked 'don't show again' is gone for good: on 2026-10-05 to 10-07 the mount driver refused every guide pulse (thousands) and PHD2 showed nothing because PulseGuideFailedAlertEnabled was 0. Read from PHD2's Confirm/<profile> registry key.
rows.fix: PHD2 Advanced Settings (Brain) > Global tab: reset the 'don't ask / show again' messages so silenced alerts show again (or, with PHD2 closed, delete the listed <Name>AlertEnabled values under HKCU Software > StarkLabs > PHDGuidingV2 > Confirm > <profile id>).
rows.note: 1 silenced: PulseGuideFailedAlertEnabled; PulseGuideFailedAlertEnabled = 0 hid every 'PulseGuide command to mount has failed' alert (2026-10-05 to 10-07: every pulse refused, PHD2 showed nothing)

rows.label: Dark library or defect map auto-loaded
rows.why: PHD2 loads the dark library or the defect map when it connects; either one keeps hot pixels out of the guide frames.
rows.fix: Darks menu: auto-load the dark library (or the bad-pixel map).
rows.desired: dark library or defect map auto-loaded

rows.label: Guide log says 'have dark'
rows.why: The dark library must be loaded, not just present on disk.
rows.fix: Darks menu: use dark library.
rows.stale_why: PHD2 settings changed 2026-10-13, after this guide log

rows.label: NINA settle threshold
rows.why: Settle is in guide pixels: 1.5 px at 0.25 arcsec/px is only 0.4 arcsec, so dithers time out.
rows.fix: NINA Options > Equipment > Guider: settle pixels equal to 0.5 to 1.0 arcsec at the guide scale.
rows.note: nina: no guider settings in the NINA profile

rows.label: NINA settle timeout (s)
rows.why: Under a minute a normal dither settle at 3248 mm times out.
rows.fix: NINA Options > Equipment > Guider: settle timeout 60 s or more.
rows.note: nina: no guider settings in the NINA profile

rows.label: Bisque driver: use DirectGuide
rows.why: Without DirectGuide TheSky can drop ASCOM PulseGuide (PHD2 users report it unchecking itself), so pulses never move the mount.
rows.fix: Bisque ASCOM driver settings: tick 'use DirectGuide'.
rows.note: driver flag location not known yet: check it by hand; ascom: driver flag names not known yet

rows.label: Bisque driver: Can Get Pointing State
rows.why: PHD2 needs the pier side to flip the calibration; the guide log must never say Pier side = Unknown.
rows.fix: Bisque ASCOM driver settings: tick 'Can Get Pointing State'.
rows.note: driver flag location not known yet: check it by hand; ascom: driver flag names not known yet

rows.label: RA aggressiveness
rows.why: Shown for reference: how much of each RA error the algorithm corrects per frame (PHD2 default 70% for Lowpass2 / Hysteresis).
rows.fix: Brain > Algorithms > RA: aggressiveness (change only after a Guiding Assistant run).

rows.label: Guide camera
rows.why: Only the OAG guide camera may guide: the GP678C until the swap, then the ZWO ASI174MM Mini (the [[camera]] tables); the AP26CC is the piggyback imaging camera and the AP26MC is the main camera.
rows.fix: PHD2 Connect Equipment: select the OAG guide camera (GP678C, or the ASI174MM Mini after the swap), never the AP26CC or AP26MC.
rows.note: OGMA GP678C: its rows are applied
rows.desired: one of OGMA GP678C, ZWO ASI174MM Mini

rows.label: Guide pixel scale ("/px)
rows.why: PHD2's scale must be the connected camera's pixel size x binning over the OAG focal length: 0.254 for the GP678C at bin 2, 0.372 for the ASI174MM Mini at bin 1. A miss means the profile kept the old camera's pixel size or a wrong focal length.
rows.fix: Brain > Camera: the camera's pixel size and binning; Brain > Global: focal length 3248 mm.

rows.label: Camera bit depth
rows.why: In 8-bit mode every star reads saturated (Max ADU 255): on 09-26 100% of frames were flagged saturated at SNR 17 and the centroids were poor.
rows.fix: PHD2 Connect Equipment > camera properties (the gear next to the camera): 16-bit. Not in PHD2's API; a profile write needs phd2_audit_autofix.

rows.label: Saturation detected by Max ADU
rows.why: With saturation by Max ADU at the 16-bit ceiling PHD2 flags only truly clipped stars.
rows.fix: Brain > Camera: saturation by Max ADU, value 65535.

rows.label: Max ADU
rows.why: With Max ADU 255 on a 16-bit camera every star reads saturated: the 09-26 cause. It must match the bit depth (65535 at 16-bit).
rows.fix: Brain > Camera: saturation by Max ADU, value 65535 (16-bit).

rows.label: Camera pixel size (um)
rows.why: PHD2 turns pixels into arcsec with this; a wrong value skews every RMS number, min-move and the calibration step.
rows.fix: Brain > Camera: pixel size 2.0 um (GP678C; the ASI174MM Mini row says 5.86).

rows.label: Auto exposure off
rows.why: Auto exposure changes the exposure under the dark library and the hot-pixel map; a fixed exposure keeps them valid.
rows.fix: Exposure dropdown: a fixed value, not Auto.

rows.label: Star mass change tolerance
rows.why: At 50% seeing and thin cloud trip it constantly: 216 of 305 drops on 09-26 were 'mass changed'.
rows.fix: Brain > Guiding: star mass detection off (or 80 to 100%).

rows.label: Minimum star HFD (px)
rows.why: A floor of 1.5 to 2.0 px keeps PHD2 from auto-selecting a hot pixel as a star (the PS-91 non-star lock).
rows.fix: Brain > Guiding: minimum star HFD 1.5 px.

rows.label: Multi-star guiding
rows.why: Averaging several stars halves the centroid noise from seeing on a small OAG field.
rows.fix: Brain > Guiding: use multiple stars.

rows.label: RA algorithm vs periodic-error owner
rows.why: Exactly one thing may correct periodic error: ProTrack / TheSky PEC (pe_owner=protrack) or PHD2 PPEC (pe_owner=phd2_ppec), never both.
rows.fix: Brain > Algorithms: RA Hysteresis or Lowpass2 when ProTrack owns PE; Predictive PEC only when pe_owner=phd2_ppec.
rows.desired: not Predictive PEC (ProTrack owns periodic error)

rows.label: Dec algorithm
rows.why: Resist Switch only reverses Dec after a sustained trend, which suits a well-aligned Paramount; Lowpass2 in Dec flip-flopped on 09-26.
rows.fix: Brain > Algorithms: Dec algorithm Resist Switch.

rows.label: Dec guide mode
rows.why: Auto corrects Dec both ways; North or South only is for a known one-way drift, Off stops Dec guiding.
rows.fix: Brain > Algorithms: Dec guide mode Auto.

rows.label: Dec backlash compensation off
rows.why: The Guiding Assistant measured 0 ms backlash on the Paramount; compensation would only add overshoot.
rows.fix: Brain > Algorithms: backlash compensation off.

rows.label: Stop guiding when the mount slews
rows.why: PHD2 stops guiding when the mount slews instead of chasing the star across the sky (NINA also stops guiding before a slew, this is the safety net).
rows.fix: Advanced > Mount: stop guiding when mount slews.

rows.label: Auto restore calibration
rows.why: Lets every target after the PS-93 calibration reuse it instead of calibrating again.
rows.fix: Brain > Guiding: auto restore calibration on.

rows.label: Dec compensation
rows.why: Scales the RA rate by cos(Dec) so one calibration near Dec 0 serves every target.
rows.fix: Advanced > Mount: use Dec compensation.

rows.label: Focal length (mm)
rows.why: The OAG sees through the RC16 at 3248 mm; 09-18 ran with 600 mm, a 5.4x scale error in every number PHD2 printed.
rows.fix: Brain > Global: focal length 3248 mm (select the OAG profile).

rows.label: Guide speed matches the mount
rows.why: PHD2 sizes every pulse from the guide speed; if TheSky guides at a different rate every correction is off by that ratio (the PS-92 WARN case).
rows.fix: Match TheSky's autoguide rate and the ASCOM driver guide rate, then recalibrate.
rows.stale_why: PHD2 settings changed 2026-10-13, after this guide log

rows.label: Mount guide output enabled
rows.why: With guide output off PHD2 measures the star and reports Guiding but sends no pulses, so every long sub trails while the dashboard says guiding. (Not the 2026-10-06 cause: that night output was on and the mount driver refused each pulse; guard D7 pages on either.)
rows.fix: PHD2 Advanced Settings > Guiding tab > Shared Parameters: tick Enable mount guide output.

rows.label: Dark library
rows.why: Without darks hot pixels look like stars; 09-26 guided with no dark or defect map from 20:29 to 21:53.
rows.fix: Tools > Dark library: build darks covering 1 to 4 s at the current gain and binning, roof closed.
rows.desired: covers 1 to 4 s (and the current exposure), under 30 days old

rows.label: Bad-pixel (defect) map
rows.why: The defect map removes hot pixels for good; the guide logs say 'no defect map'.
rows.fix: Tools > Bad-pixel map: build one at the final gain and binning.

rows.label: TheSky TCP scripting reachable
rows.why: TheSky's TCP server is how PhotonScript can read ProTrack and the mount state directly.
rows.fix: TheSky: Tools > TCP Server: listen for connections (port 3040).
